desc: Read the input values: K, S, and T.
Implement a function to compute the bounded Levenshtein distance with a limit of K.

Use two arrays (or vectors) to store the current and previous rows of the DP table, initializing the first row and column appropriately but clamping values at K+1 to avoid overflow and unnecessary computation.

Iterate through the characters of S and T, computing the DP values only within the band defined by K. For each cell, compute the minimum of insert, delete, and replace costs, adding 1 if characters don't match.
After each row computation, check if the minimum value in that row exceeds K. If it does, return "No" early.
After processing all characters, check if the final computed distance is <= K. If yes, print "Yes"; otherwise, print "No".
